summary: Build budget control, cash planning, and IPSAS reporting skills in this advanced 5-day PFM course. Train with practical tools and templates.
lede: Public financial management training covers the practical work of planning, executing, controlling, and reporting public resources. It is for budget officers, treasury analysts, public-sector accountants, auditors, and finance managers who support the budget cycle. Through applied exercises, participants practise developing budget ceilings and cash plans, tracking commitments and expenditure controls, reviewing IPSAS-aligned reports, and assessing control gaps and fiscal risks.
audienceIntro: This public financial management training is built for professionals who already work inside the budget cycle and need sharper tools for execution, control, reporting, and reform delivery.
prerequisites: Participants should already have a working understanding of public sector budgeting, treasury operations, accounting, or audit processes. Prior exposure to budget cycles, basic financial reports, and public expenditure controls will help you get the most from the exercises, which are set at an advanced operational level. No programming is required, but you should be prepared to work with spreadsheets, budget templates, variance schedules, and reporting formats used in public financial management.
